config.title: Event Typing

intro.title: Event Typing
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple form with a text input and a submit button to learn how to properly type events in React with TypeScript. You'll explore the core concept of event typing, which ensures your event handlers are type-safe and prevent common runtime errors. The main technologies involved are React functional components, TypeScript interfaces, and React's built-in event types like React.ChangeEvent and React.FormEvent. By the end, you'll know how to access event properties safely and understand why TypeScript helps catch mistakes early in your development process.
intro.usecase: Typing events is essential in professional React applications where user interactions drive functionality. In e-commerce checkout forms, proper event typing ensures address fields capture correct input types and validation errors. Dashboard filter panels rely on typed change events to safely update multiple data visualizations simultaneously. Interactive data tables use typed click events to handle row selections while maintaining type safety across complex state updates.

objectives: Apply TypeScript event types to React event handler functions
Construct typed event handlers for common DOM events like click and change
Initialize form state with proper types and bind it to controlled components
Manipulate event objects to extract typed values from form inputs
Integrate generic event types with custom handler functions
Configure event handlers to update component state with type-safe values
Render interactive UI elements with fully typed event handling

steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.instruction: Import React and useState from 'react' to use React components and state management.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in the necessary modules from the 'react' package.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: importing modules
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: The imports are added at the top of the file, enabling the use of React and the useState hook.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're importing both React and useState from the 'react' package.
steps.feedbackWrong: That's not quite right. You need to import React and useState from 'react' to proceed.

steps.title: Create main component with TypeScript
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named App that returns a JSX element, typed with React.FC.
steps.hint: Define App using either function App() {} or const App: React.FC = () => {}. Make sure it returns a JSX element like a div.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';

// Create the App component here
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component is defined with React.FC typing and returns a JSX element.
successCriteria: App is defined as a functional component with React.FC typing and returns a JSX element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure App is typed with React.FC and returns a JSX element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The App component isn't defined correctly. Check that it uses React.FC typing and returns JSX.

steps.title: Initialize state with typed value
steps.instruction: Inside your component, use useState to initialize a state variable named 'text' with an empty string as its initial value. Ensure the state is typed as string.
steps.hint: Call useState with an empty string '' as the initial argument. TypeScript will infer the type automatically, but you can also explicitly type it: useState<string>('').
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: typed state initialization
const [count, setCount] = useState<number>(0);
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a typed state variable 'text' initialized to an empty string.
successCriteria: The useState hook is called with an empty string, and the state variable 'text' is typed as string.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're calling useState with an empty string and that the state is typed as string.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've used useState with an empty string initial value and typed it as string.

steps.title: Define typed event handler function
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, define a function called handleChange that takes a React.ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement> parameter and updates the text state with event.target.value.
steps.hint: Remember to use the setText function from useState to update the state. The function should be defined before the return statement.
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have a handleChange function that properly types the event parameter and updates the state with the input value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that your function has the correct parameter type and properly updates the state with event.target.value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handleChange function isn't quite right. Make sure it takes a React.ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement> parameter and calls setText(event.target.value) inside the function body.

steps.title: Add basic structure with div container
steps.instruction: Return a div element from your App component to serve as the container for the UI.
steps.hint: Replace the current return statement with a JSX div element.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now returns a JSX div element, providing a container for the UI elements you'll add later.
successCriteria: The App component returns a JSX div element
The return statement is updated from null to

steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're returning a JSX div element from the component.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've replaced the return statement with a JSX div element.

steps.title: Add heading to display lesson title
steps.instruction: Inside the div container in your App component, add an h1 element with the text 'Event Typing Lesson'.
steps.hint: Place the h1 element as the first child inside the opening and closing div tags.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding a heading element

Welcome to the Lesson
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will now display a heading with the lesson title inside the div container.
successCriteria: An h1 element with the text 'Event Typing Lesson' is added inside the div container.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the lesson title heading.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added an h1 element, but check that the text content matches 'Event Typing Lesson' exactly.
steps.feedbackWrong: The heading wasn't added correctly. Make sure to add an h1 element with the exact text 'Event Typing Lesson' inside the div.

steps.title: Add input element with typed onChange
steps.instruction: Add an input element with type='text' inside the div container, and wire its onChange event to the handleChange function.
steps.hint: Use the <input> tag with type='text' and onChange={handleChange}.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding an input with an event handler
<input type="text" onChange={handleInputChange} />
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will now contain an input element that triggers the handleChange function when its value changes.
successCriteria: An input element with type='text' and onChange={handleChange} is added inside the div container.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added an input, but make sure it has type='text' and onChange={handleChange}.
steps.feedbackWrong: The input element is missing or not correctly wired to the handleChange function.

steps.title: Add button with typed onClick handler
steps.instruction: Add a button element after the input that clears the text state when clicked. Use an onClick handler with the correct TypeScript event type.
steps.hint: Create a button with an onClick prop that calls a function. The function should call setText with an empty string. Remember to type the event parameter as React.MouseEvent<HTMLButtonElement>.
steps.expectedOutcome: A button appears after the input field. When clicked, it clears the text in the input field by resetting the text state to an empty string.
successCriteria: Button element is added with onClick handler that calls a function to clear text state. The click handler function has proper TypeScript event typing.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a button, but check: Did you include the onClick handler with proper TypeScript typing? The handler should call setText('') to clear the state.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button or its click handler is missing or incorrect. Add a button element with an onClick handler that clears the text state when clicked.

steps.title: Export the component
steps.instruction: Export the App component as the default export so it can be used by other parts of the application.
steps.hint: Use the 'export default' syntax at the end of the file.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component is exported as the default export, making it available for use elsewhere.
successCriteria: The App component is exported using 'export default App'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
